scenes.text: Rohan buys some pencils at ₹5 and some erasers at ₹3 and pays ₹40.
He writes 5x + 3y = 40 — one equation, two unknowns. How many possibilities are there?

steps.title: Definition and standard form
steps.body: An equation that can be written as **ax + by + c = 0**, where a, b, c are real numbers and **a and b are not both zero**, is a linear equation in two variables x and y. 'Linear' because each variable has power 1 (its graph is a straight line).

steps.title: Solved: one-variable equations in two-variable form
Solved: write as an equation
steps.body: 'The cost of a notebook is twice the cost of a pen.' Let notebook = ₹x, pen = ₹y: x = 2y ⇒ **x − 2y = 0**.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Forgetting to move every term to one side before reading c (sign of c changes).
- Calling xy + x = 3 linear — the term xy has degree 2.
- Thinking b = 0 is not allowed: a or b may be zero, just not both.

activity.prompt: Match each equation with (a, b, c) in ax + by + c = 0

quiz.q: Which is a linear equation in two variables?
quiz.why: 3x − 2y = 7 has both variables to the power 1, so it is linear. Terms like xy, x² or 1/y make an equation non-linear.

quiz.q: In 2x − 5y = 10 written as ax + by + c = 0, c =
quiz.why: Move 10 to the left side: 2x − 5y − 10 = 0. So c = −10.

quiz.q: y = 3 written in two variables is
quiz.why: y = 3 can be written as 0·x + 1·y − 3 = 0, with a = 0 and b = 1. It is a linear equation in two variables.
The sum of two numbers x and y is x + y, so the equation is x + y = 27. The difference or product would give other equations.

quiz.q: In ax + by + c = 0 the condition is
options: a and b not both zero
quiz.why: In ax + by + c = 0, a and b must not both be zero. Otherwise there would be no variables in the equation.

scenes.text: Pens cost ₹10 and notebooks ₹20; Meena spends exactly ₹100.
(10, 0), (6, 2), (2, 4), (0, 5)… She finds many correct baskets — every one is a solution.

steps.title: What a solution is
steps.body: A **solution** is a pair (x, y) that makes both sides equal. A linear equation in two variables has **infinitely many** solutions (each one a point on its straight line). To find solutions: choose any x, solve for y.

steps.title: Solved: find k
steps.body: If x = 2, y = 1 is a solution of 2x + 3y = k, then k = 4 + 3 = **7**.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Writing only one solution when 'infinitely many' is the correct description.
- Substituting x and y the wrong way round: (a, b) always means x = a, y = b.
- Arithmetic with fractions — choose x values that make y a whole number.

activity.prompt: Find y if (3, y) is a solution of 2x + 3y = 18

quiz.why: A linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions, as each value of x gives a value of y. So 2x + 5y = 10 has infinitely many.

quiz.q: Which is a solution of x + y = 5?
quiz.why: For (3, 2), 3 + 2 = 5, so it satisfies x + y = 5. The other pairs do not add up to 5.
For (1, 3), y = 3 = 3 × 1, so it satisfies y = 3x. The others do not give y = 3x.
Put x = 0 in 2x + y = 7: y = 7.
Put (2, 0): 2 − 2(0) = 2, which is not 4. So (2, 0) is not a solution.

scenes.text: An auto charges ₹15 for the first km and ₹8 for each further km.
Asha writes y = 15 + 8(x − 1) — a linear equation that turns a fare card into maths.

steps.title: Method
steps.body:
1. Name the unknowns (x = …, y = …) with units.
2. Translate each phrase: 'twice' → 2×, 'more than' → +, 'is' → =.
3. Simplify to ax + by + c = 0.
4. Find solutions that make sense (often only whole, non-negative values).

steps.title: Solved: taxi fare
steps.body:
Fare: ₹8 for first km and ₹5 per km after. Distance x km, fare ₹y.
y = 8 + 5(x − 1) ⇒ y = 5x + 3 ⇒ **5x − y + 3 = 0**. For 10 km: y = 53.

steps.title: Solved: donations
steps.body: Two students together contribute ₹100 to a relief fund. x + y = 100. Solutions include (50, 50), (60, 40), (100, 0) — many.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Charging the first km twice in fare problems (use x − 1 for 'each further km').
- Ignoring units or meaning (negative pencils!).

quiz.why: The perimeter of a rectangle is 2(length + breadth), so 2x + 2y = 40.

quiz.why: The cost of rice is 12x and of dal is 40y. Together they are ₹200, so 12x + 40y = 200.
F = (9/5) × 100 + 32 = 180 + 32 = 212. This is the boiling point of water in °F.
Put x = 4: y = 5(4) + 3 = 20 + 3 = 23, so the fare is ₹23.

scenes.text: Kiran plots (0, 7), (7, 0), (3, 4) for x + y = 7 on graph paper.
They line up perfectly. Every solution is on the line, and every point on the line is a solution.

steps.title: Graphing
steps.body:
Make a table of 2–3 solutions, plot them, join with a ruler and extend. The graph of ax + by + c = 0 is always a **straight line**.
- x = a is a line parallel to the y-axis; y = b is parallel to the x-axis.
- y = mx passes through the origin.

steps.title: Edition note
steps.body: In recent rationalised NCERT books the graph sections of this chapter may be trimmed; the skill is still essential for Class 10 'Pair of Linear Equations'.

steps.title: Solved: graph of 2x + y = 6
steps.body: x = 0 → y = 6; x = 3 → y = 0; x = 1 → y = 4. Plot (0, 6), (3, 0), (1, 4); join. It cuts the y-axis at (0, 6) and the x-axis at (3, 0).

steps.title: Solved: lines through a point
steps.body: How many lines pass through (2, 14)? **Infinitely many**, e.g. y = 7x, x + y = 16, 7x − y = 0.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Plotting only two points (use a third as a check).
- Thinking x = 3 is a point — on the plane it is a vertical line.

y = 3 is parallel to the y-axis

x = −2 is a vertical line, as x is always −2 whatever y is. So it is parallel to the y-axis.

quiz.why: For (2, 4), y = 4 = 2 + 2, so it lies on y = x + 2. The others do not satisfy it.

quiz.why: The graph of a linear equation in two variables is a straight line. A parabola or circle comes from a quadratic equation.

questions.why: 2x + y = 5 has both variables to the power 1, so it is linear. √x, x² and xy make an equation non-linear.

questions.why: x + y = 4 is a linear equation in two variables, which has infinitely many solutions, such as (1, 3) and (2, 2).
In ax + by + c = 0, b is the coefficient of y. For 3x − 7y + 2 = 0, b = −7.

questions.why: x = 5 can be written as x + 0·y − 5 = 0, with a = 1, b = 0 and c = −5.

questions.why: For (2, 1), 2(2) − 1 = 3, so it satisfies the equation. The others do not.

Assertion (A): (1, 1) is a solution of x + y = 2. Reason (R): a linear equation in two variables has a unique solution.
options: Both true; R does not explain A
questions.why: The assertion is true: (1, 1) satisfies x + y = 2, as 1 + 1 = 2. The reason is false, since a linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions, not a unique one.

questions.q: 'The number of boys (x) is 5 less than twice the number of girls (y)':
questions.why: Twice the number of girls minus 5 gives the number of boys: x = 2y − 5. 'Less than' means subtract from twice the number.

Graph of x + 2y = 8 meets the y-axis at

questions.why: Put y = 11 in y = 3x + 2: 11 = 3x + 2, so 3x = 9 and x = 3.

questions.why: Put x = 9 in y = 4x + 6: y = 36 + 6 = 42, so the charge is ₹42.

questions.why: Set F = C: C = 9C/5 + 32, so −4C/5 = 32 and C = −40. At −40, both scales read the same.

questions.why: For (0, 0), the equation must have 0 on the right. x − 4y = 0 gives 0 − 0 = 0, so it works. The others give 1.
